Refutation target under test (Stop 1 comment 5858625914): It is acceptable that a full-story PR must write Tracking #N while the brief is still in xbrief/active, because --allow-close is correctly refused until scope:complete and Tracking remains the safe default, even though GitHub then leaves the finished issue open after squash-merge.

## Open-after-merge acceptability does not bind
blocks-the-design
Evidence: At pin 0040c878, `refuseAllowCloseWhileRunning` in `packages/core/src/pr-closing-keywords/main.ts` fails `--allow-close N` when `listActiveRunningBriefs` still tracks N; pre-pr policy defaults Tracking/Refs. Separately, closed #4824 / CHANGELOG and `closeOriginsAfterLeftoverComplete` in `packages/core/src/swarm/finalize-cohort.ts` treat a still-open origin after leftover-complete land as refused DONE ("Tracking/Refs does not auto-close"), with tests that PATCH-close Tracking bodies. Live REST: #4824 closed; successor #4919 still open for hand finalize of merged Tracking stories. Issue #4864 body records the 2026-09-22 hand-close cohort.
Failure mode: Binding the target as written would ratify "finished story stays open after squash-merge" as acceptable design, contradicting the already-shipped finalize DONE contract and the measured defect this issue was filed for.
Disposition: Retract the acceptability-of-open-leftover half before any bind. Keep the gate-sound half (#3015 intent + #4628 running-brief refuse + Tracking as default while the brief is active).

## Split PR-open Tracking from post-merge close ownership
sharpens-framing
Evidence: Inventory at the pin shows two seams, not one: (1) PR-open body lint (`pr-closing-keywords` + pre-pr Tracking default + Grok `stop-at: pr-open` forbidding pre-merge `scope:complete`); (2) post-merge origin-close already on `swarm:finalize-cohort` after leftover-complete land (#4824/#4937), while #3791/`complete-cohort` sweep moves briefs and does not close GitHub issues. Wanted text on #4864 asks to record full-story intent at PR open and apply close when the brief leaves `active/`, without dropping #3015/#4628.
Failure mode: A successor lean that only restates "Tracking while active is correct" leaves P2 (open after merge) unowned. A lean that invents a second close authority beside finalize, or that reverses #4628 so Closes can land while the brief is running, splits or weakens shared issue-close lifecycle authority (injection/swarm lens).
Disposition: Before bind, name the post-merge owner explicitly—compose with or extend `closeOriginsAfterLeftoverComplete` / #4919 finalize path, or a recorded full-story intent consumed when the brief leaves `active/`—and keep `--allow-close` refused while running. Do not make Tracking illegal for partial PRs.

## Protected umbrella and closeout gates already constrain Closes
footnote
Evidence: `isProtectedStayingOpenUmbrella` skips origin-close for umbrella/protected labels in finalize-cohort; `pr-closeout-attestable` fails merge when structured closing refs would close an unattested running brief. Live `--pr` intent-fail is skipped unless `--allow-close` is passed (`main.ts`), so local `--body-file` pre-pr remains the hard Tracking force while active.
Failure mode: None for bind if the lean keeps partial-PR / umbrella non-close and does not treat #3791 as the GitHub close fix.
Disposition: Carry-forward constraint only; no harvest change by itself.

## Verdict
The refutation target does not survive. The composition that forces Tracking while the brief is active is sound and must stay. The claim that leaving the finished GitHub issue open after squash-merge is an acceptable terminal state is what fails, and that is the grain a Bound remedy must own.

metadata.issueBody:
# bug(pr): a finished story cannot say Closes while its brief is still active

## Summary

A pull request that is the whole issue cannot pass the closing-keyword check with `Closes` / `Fixes` / `Resolves`. The brief is still in `xbrief/active` when the body is written, `--allow-close` is refused, and the only body that passes is `Tracking`. GitHub then leaves the issue open. Nothing after the merge closes it.

Tracking remains the right default for a partial pull request. This is the full-story case only.

## What happens

1. The closing-keyword check (#3015) rejects a real `Closes` / `Fixes` / `Resolves #N` unless the pull request is the full issue and the check is run with `--allow-close N`.
2. #4628 refuses `--allow-close N` while issue N still has a running brief in `xbrief/active`.
3. A Grok implement leaf stops when the pull request opens and must not `scope:complete` before the merge, so that brief is still active when the body is written.
4. `Tracking #N` is the only body that passes. GitHub auto-closes only on `Closes` / `Fixes` / `Resolves`.
5. After the merge, the brief sweep (#3791) moves `active/` to `completed/`. It does not close the GitHub issue.

On 2026-09-22 a cohort of finished stories stayed open for that reason and had to be closed by hand after the squash: #4522, #4707, #4812, #4819, #4839, #4841, #4843, #4844, #4846, #4847, #4854. The leaves were also told to write Tracking. That instruction made the miss certain. The product still cannot say Closes in this window.

## Wanted

A pull request that is the full issue can be marked so GitHub closes it, without completing the brief before the merge and without letting a partial pull request auto-close an umbrella.

One shape that fits the current gates: record the full-story intent at PR open, and apply the close when the brief leaves `active/` after the merge. `--allow-close` while the brief is still active stays refused.

## Not this

- Do not make Tracking illegal.
- Do not drop #3015 or #4628.
- Do not treat #3791 as this fix. That issue sweeps the brief. It does not close the GitHub issue.

Refs #3015, #4628, #3791

expected_outputs: full-story post-merge origin close without hand PATCH
